plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Pale lilac-pink goblets rise straight from bare soil, with no leaves in sight. They carpet damp meadows and woodland edges just as autumn begins to turn.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid-autumn (roughly September to October)
plants.location: Meadows and open woodland across Western and Central Europe, including the UK, France and Germany
plants.funFact: Despite its name, this is not a true crocus. It is a member of the lily family, and every part of it contains colchicine, a toxic compound. Plant breeders use colchicine to double the chromosomes of other plants.

plants.name: Symphyotrichum novae-angliae
plants.description: Dense clusters of daisy-like flowers with golden centers light up prairies, roadsides and gardens. They arrive just as most other wildflowers are fading, and they draw in late-season butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer through autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, from New England to the Great Plains
plants.funFact: Monarch butterflies stop to feed on its nectar during their autumn migration to Mexico. Its flower heads also close up at night and on cloudy days.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole streets turn lavender-blue when this tree flowers. Trumpet-shaped blooms cover the branches and then drop to form a purple carpet underfoot.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November)
plants.location: Cities in the Southern Hemisphere, such as Pretoria in South Africa, Sydney and Brisbane in Australia, and Buenos Aires in Argentina
plants.funFact: The tree comes from South America, but Pretoria is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of its tens of thousands of them. Their bloom is a local sign of spring.
